text_fidelity_a:
Auoxer Fitness Exercise Weighted Hoola Hoop, Detachable and Size Adjustable Design, Lose Weight Fast by Fun Way, Fat Burning Healthy Model Sports Life This is the third hula hoop I’ve owned that breaks down this way. I also own an empower fitness hoop (it’s the pink and orange hoop in my picture while this hoop is the pink and grey hoop) and gave away a hoopologie one (couldn’t stand how squeaky it was).

I’d put this in the middle. The empower fitness one is made of a thicker more sturdy tubing. But this is perfectly fine especially for beginners who don’t want to spend much.

I would ignore advice about going to a toy store to get a cheaper hoop. This is very reasonably priced for adult hoops. There’s a video out there of olympic athletes trying with those kid hoops. It was a failure. Those hoops are designed for kid sized bodies and even athletes on the snaller side struggle with kid hoops. When starting out most hooping sites suggest you have a hoop that comes to about your waist when resting on the floor.

As far as weighted hoops go, this is just right, not too heavy (have never seen any proof that weighted is better and many believe it’s not). If they’re too heavy most recommend using them for only 10-20 minutes, lighter hoops get no such warnings.

So far so good with this one. I will update if my opinion changes but I would put this as a good starter hoop. In addition to the three collapsible hoops I’ve used another non-weighted hoop. Have never bruised but bruising isn’t uncommon when starting out so I’d advise starting out with a few minutes here and there to build up a tolerance if you bruise easily.
text_fidelity_b: Auoxer Fitness Exercise Weighted Hoola Hoop, Detachable and Size Adjustable Design, Lose Weight Fast by Fun Way, Fat Burning Healthy Model Sports Life

text_fidelity_a: SUUNTO Spartan Trainer Wrist HR Multisport GPS Watch I’ll admit that I’ve never owned a full-blown trainer watch before, so the only thing I have to compare to is a Fitbit Charge2 fitness tracker. They’re really two different kinds of watches, although they have some similar features. First, and I’m not really comparing to the Fitbit, I found the Suunto a little heavy, at 67 grams or 2.36 ounces. I’m not sure how that compares to other similar watches. I do, however, think I’ll get used to it. One of the main initial conclusions is that, while the buttons on the watch are fairly intuitive, trying to learn about the detailed features was not that easy. I want to the website and it was just a difficult experience trying to get to the info. I didn’t find a way to get a PDF downloaded for offline use, although there may be one. Conclusion on ease of website use is, it’s not easy to use. There’s a lot of info there, but it’s not that easy to get to the User Manual that you need, and once there, I really didn’t think the explanations were that easy to understand. The Movescount app wasn’t that much better. Although I set the Units to “Imperial” I still can’t get the Activity distance measurements off of Km  and onto miles. I like the alerts from phone to watch such as text messages. I don’t like the fact that, while this is a Heart Rate watch, you can’t seem to see HR on the watch unless you’re in an Activity mode. But when you are, the real time graph thing is pretty cool. I think that this watch will do a lot of things. I just don’t think it’s the most user-friendly total package that it could be.
text_fidelity_b: SUUNTO Spartan Trainer Wrist HR Multisport GPS Watch

text_fidelity_a:
ESEE Lite Machete Micarta Handles and Sheath This is by far the best machete I have owned and used during my 33 years living in Southwest Florida. I am a big knife collector and ran across this machete by chance when researching other big knives. Previously I had used several Cold Steel machetes which were quite satisfactory--until I discovered and started using the Esee Lite Machete.

Yes, the price point is higher, but what you get is a long, well-balanced, razor sharp, light weight, and flexible blade that cuts through 3" to 5" limbs like the proverbial "knife through butter". Besides that, all Esee products are guaranteed for life. While I haven't abused one to the breaking point yet--although I've tried--all you have to do is send it back to the company for repair or replacement (at the option of the company).

I take two of them into the wetlands with me when cutting Brazilian Pepper trees. Sharpening them is simple with the proper stone and they hold their edge far longer than lesser machetes made of softer steel. You can use them for hours with minimal fatigue because of the good grip, fine balance and light weight. The only better knife that I can compare it to is my Busse Nuclear Fusion Battle Mistress which costs upwards of $500.00. However, the NFBM is considerably heavier and has a thicker blade. This causes shallower cuts and quicker arm fatigue.

So ante up a few extra bucks and enjoy the superior cutting power of the Esee Machete. You will never buy another cheap machete because you will be spoiled by your new Esee.

NOTE 02/15/15: I finally found a drawback to the Esee Lite. The areas I work in are so thick that if you drop the machete or put it down and forget where you put it, it's almost impossible to find. So now I spray the handle with fluorescent orange paint which makes it much easier to see and recover.
text_fidelity_b: ESEE Lite Machete Micarta Handles and Sheath

text_fidelity_a:
Tour Edge Men's TGS Triple Grind Sole Wedge Keep in mind I received it today and haven't used it much, but I did hit some side by side shots with my CG16 wedge of the same loft. Distance was virtually identical. I definitely saw the Tour launched the ball higher. I'm sure that's related to the spin increase compared to a 10 year old wedge. That being said, I certainly don't have any complaints.

I really like the grind. I was able to play with some knock downs from tight lies, hit full shots from the back and front of my stance, even hit a few wide open flops (yeah I know a 52 really isn't the club). In all cases I was able to make clean contact.

The feel isn't what I would call "pure", but it was fine. A bit clicky to me, but as far as my game goes I am not going to consider that a negative. Some more accomplished players may see that as a bad thing.

The lie isn't right for me, I seemed to pull most shots with a slight draw. The opposite of my current clubs as I normally fade them. We will see how that plays on the course, but that's on me, not the club.

Bottom line: Let's face it, a functional club for an extremely affordable price is something we all can use. This club fits the situation perfectly.
text_fidelity_b: Tour Edge Men's TGS Triple Grind Sole Wedge

Everything you need to assemble this item is included in one handy little case. Extra screws, Allen wrench, 2 extra rubber bands, and steel ammo. Because of how this is constructed, it took me a little longer to get the bands connected and secured, but once it was done it looked good and was ready. Or so I thought. As I started holding it more and aiming it, I felt something protruding from the handle and looking closely saw it was the eagle design and the bottom tail of the eagle was sticking out a little when it should have been level with the slingshot surface. I tried to fix this by hammering the slingshot protected with a towel, only to find the entire eagle design moves every time I tried to use the slingshot. That metal protrusion is really a safety issue.

I then went ahead and wore gloves to try out the slingshot. The bands are really nice and stretchy and the stainless ammo balls were perfect for practice. The slingshot shoots pretty well and is comfortable to hold. Even though the handle is kind of short, the large metal loop makes it easier to hold because it conforms better to my hand. I do like this slingshot, but feel something needs to be done about the eagle design and how it moves such that the sharp edges stick out.

text_fidelity_a:
CAP Barbell Flat/Incline/Decline Bench PROS:
- Easy to set up. I don't know why some previous reviewers say it takes 2 hours with 2 people. It took me one person (myself) about an hour with 2 wrenches. The manual has crappy pictures, but as long as you can read English and follow instructions then the written instructions are all you really need (while occasionally looking at the picture to get the general idea). The bench is very sturdy and sits level. It weighs about 25lbs, so it's not exactly light weight. All of the required hardware was present and some of the easier steps were already performed (e.g. the plastic end-caps).
- Versatile. There are leg pads for situps and the backrest angles from flat to about 30 degrees to nearly 90 degrees. It does not recline below horizontal.
- Price. Can't beat this quality for less than a Grant.

CONS:
-Smell. Ok. Yes, the rubber pads do smell like, well, rubber. It is fading, but if smells really affect you then look elsewhere.
-Length. This thing is short! I'm 5'8" and I just barely fit on this thing. Unless I wrap my legs over the top padded bar, my head is completely off the backrest. This can be uncomfortable during situps and chest presses. The width is adequate.
-Design flaw. The space between the sitting pad and the backrest is slightly larger than is comfortable and during situps you kind of sink into the space. I'm going to try using a towel to fill it and see if that helps.

Of note, there are two J-hooks on either side of the bench, which are meant to hold small dumbbells. If you use anything over 10 lbs, I doubt these will be used. They can hold a towel or water bottle however. They should have skipped the dumbbell holder and lengthened the backrest.

To that end I grabbed these YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddles to take instead of a SUP paddle with my new SUP. A couple things: 1. we have done both kayaking and SUPing, but always in a group, so we are new at having our own and beginners with limited knowledge of what is good vs. not. This is all presented from that beginners perspective. 2. While we have new SUPs and paddles, we are not able to get out for several more weeks. Between a very rainy year so far in 2021 and my recent major surgery limiting what I can do, we are getting these as a promise to ourselves and with an eye to being back out and active as soon as possible. Therefore, this review is also from having and using the paddle out of the water.

Having read about paddles and having used them in a limited way, I do find that these YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddles are a big heavier - I’ve held lighter. But it’s fine for my needs. We will get out there several times a year on salt water (mostly intercostal) and we feel this will be a good set for the setting and our ability level. It looks nice - I like the blue and black - and the materials seem solid. That said, I cannot give this a 5 star rating - it only deserves 4 stars in that putting it together - while easy - was hindered by a peg that was/is not exactly spot on. As you can see in the pics, one button went in well - easy on the first try - on both ends. The other one does not. I tried it first actually, placing it in, getting it lined up, but it is JUST-THAT-OFF (short) that it would not pop out. I tried the other end. It also did not pop out. As I am recovering from surgery I was not able to “fight it’ and had my wife. She was finally - after much effort - able to fight in into one end where it would pop out securing it into place by the pop out. Because of this 1. It’s far harder to set in place that is should and 2. makes us question it’s strength when in use. Would it too easily pop out? So to that end, 4 stars. They need to do better on lining up those pegs that keep the ends in place. It seems like a great paddle, but it needs to get together and apart quickly, easily, and stay together safely. This YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddle set is not good enough to say it does that.

text_fidelity_a: Irico Stainless Steel Tumbler, Double Wall Vacuum Insulated Travel Mugs, No Sweat with Lid, 30 Ounce I just have to say, I love this stainless tumbler.  It is 30 oz and has a pleasantly tapered shape, with smooth, comfortable indentations at the bottom third of the cup.  It keeps things very cold and hot, like other stainless vacuum tumblers, but the smooth dented grip really sets this apart.  30 oz. is too big for hot beverages (for me), but I love having cold water or even iced tea/coffee out of this one, with plenty of ice.  It is easy to stay hydrated even in steamy Northeast summers, because this preserves its cool even in the car.  I have a number of other stainless vacuum bottles/flasks/tumblers, by various other manufacturers - and this one is the nicest in my hand, by far.  While I have large hands for a woman, this should be comfortable for most every adult.  I tried another 30 oz tumbler by another manufacturer, and it is simply too big to be held comfortably (and is being sent back).  If you are in the market for a stainless vacuum tumbler that will be enjoyable to use as well as thermally effective, would suggest this one over the (many) competitors out there.  There is also a nicely fitted rubber or silicone pad inset in the base, so this sits softly on surfaces.  Due to the thermal properties, there is zero condensation - today is a 100% humidity day, and the exterior is dry as a bone even though it's filled with ice.  A keeper!  Hand wash only (like all similar ones).  Hopefully they will make it in other colors, would definitely buy another one.  And it would make a great gift for a number of people I know.

text_fidelity_a: 350W Electric Skateboard with Wireless Remote Control I am an old lady, not a skateboard person, but my neighbor is a divorced dad who gets his two boys every other weekend and because he has a roommate to help pay bills, I know he doesn't have a lot of money to spend on his kids when he gets them, so on occasion I have gotten a few things for them because I'd rather hear kids laughing and having fun than whining at their dad because he can't afford to buy them all the newest, coolest things.  So having said that, my intentions are also to benefit me, too!  I took this over before the boys were to be dropped off and he was so happy - I did apologize that I couldn't get two of them but hoped they would share.  About an hour later I heard them squealing so figured their dad had brought out this skateboard and was preparing to read them the riot act if they didn't share.  I looked up in time to see the older boy - he's maybe 10 or so - zoom past my house and the grin he had just made me laugh.  He was obviously loving the ride!  He came zooming past again and in another couple of minutes, the younger one - I think 7 or thereabouts - zoomed by.  His eyes were wide and he had the biggest grin on his face!  That's really all I wanted to see - that they liked it and I believe their dad was so happy to have a cool thing for them to play with at his house.  I mean, I can't say how it feels to be on it or anything like that, but I can say that two little boys had a fun weekend with their dad riding, I'm pretty sure, was their first ever skateboard and it was motorized and could be controlled with the remote control to boot!  If you are a grandparent or a parent of a young person (10 or younger, in my opinion), this skateboard is going to be a perfect gift for Christmas or their birthday.
text_fidelity_b: 350W Electric Skateboard with Wireless Remote Control

text_fidelity_a:
sixthreezero Electric-Bicycles Around The Block Women's Ebike, 250/500 Watt Motor, 7-Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle with Rear Rack, 26" Wheels, Multiple Colors This review is for the sixthreezero EVRYjourney Women's Step-Through 500-Watt Electric Bike

The short version is: This is a great bike, sixthreezero has great support, and I highly recommend the bike and company.

My mom has some back issues, including fused vertebrae, and over the years, the number of physical activities she's able to participate in has declined. Long family bike rides on a normal bike were no longer an option. For that reason, in February we decided to go to a local Pedego store and rent e-bikes for my mom and wife. We did a 15 mile ride, and everyone, including my mom and wife, loved it.

My mom liked it so much that she reconfirmed the prices when we got back, but it was definitely outside of her budget.

We both spent the next several months looking for an e-bike deal that was too good to say no to. There's some cheap options online, a Costco mountain e-bike, some nice bikes that are out of our budget, both online and locally, but nothing that was amazing...

Until Prime Day 2019.

sixthreezero's 250-watt bikes were on sale during Prime Day. I don't even see them available now, but it was a great deal, and I did some research before phoning my mom and telling her I think we'd found the deal she was looking for. After telling my mom about it, she ordered one, then asked if I was getting one for my wife. I was on the fence, because it's still a lot of money, until she said, "Don't think about how much you're spending per ride. Do you want to have lots of happy memories of the family riding together or are you OK without those?"

Well said, Mom. I ordered one the next day.

Now, I don't see the 250-watt bikes on Amazon anymore, but when they were here, the online documentation, both here and over at sixthreezero at the time we ordered made the basic functionality seem the same between the 250-watt and the 500-watt bicycles. The key feature both my mom and wife were looking for was the ability to pedal with adjustable resistance, but leverage the throttle with the left thumb to accelerate with the motor when needed to either catch up quickly or tackle hills without issue. (And without changing the level of pedal assistance.)

Some of our first impressions were not great. My mom's bike showed up looking amazing, and my dad assembled it without issue, but the throttle did not behave as expected. (The boost was limited to the level of pedal assist you were in.) My wife's bike showed up, but the fender and rack were both badly bent.

Before buying the bike, I saw that sixthreezero, if you bought directly from them, was willing to offer 365 day test drives, and seemed really focused on customer satisfaction. The Amazon reviews seemed positive, and the box the bike came in offered free assembly at a local bike store. (I'm not sure how that works because I've built over a dozen bikes and this bike is easy to assemble.) That said, I had a damaged bike and it didn't perform as I was expecting. I was definitely concerned when I reached out to sixthreezero.

After multiple calls, photos and a video to confirm that my 250-watt bike did not perform the way their 500-watt did (the technician I was working with only had a 500-watt readily available to troubleshoot with), they were willing to work with my mom and I to find a satisfactory proposal that would allow us to send back the 250-watt bikes and they would ship us 500-watt versions.

They were polite and reasonable throughout the process, but I was still nervous about bike number two, since the first bike did arrive with issues outside of the e-bike functionality. I was pleasantly surprised that they seem to have people working there who seem to genuinely want to make sure their customers love their bikes.

The 500-watt bike went together very easily, and after assembling and tuning the bike, I took it for a ride. The bike was a blast.

The only thing that jumped out at me as being substantially different from the Pedego my wife rode was the seat post. The Pedego had a shock in the seat post, which doesn't do a lot, but is better than nothing. I ordered a "Sunlite Pillar Suspension Seat Post, 27.2 x 350mm, Silver" from Amazon, which seemed like a good improvement to the bike, which is otherwise fantastic. (The rigid seat post makes the ride a tad rough, which is why I gave comfort 4 stars, I'd bump that to 5 with the suspension seat post.)

My wife says she finds the sixthreezero 500-watt basically the same as the Pedego. I'm sure there are differences, but the only big one we see is the price.

I can't adequately describe an e-bike in words alone, but if you have the option to rent one locally, I highly suggest you try it. It's a lot of fun. I'm not a fan of skilled cyclists tearing up mountain bike trails with heavier, faster e-bikes, nor would I advocate road bikers throw electric motors on their bikes, but the joy e-bikes are able to bring families by leveling the field for families that want to ride together is awesome. And sixthreezero's EVRYjourney cruiser is a fantastic bike for those people.

We're averaging speeds of more than half a mile per hour more as a family than we used to, and my wife comes home with a smile on her face while my kids come home having used up more energy and me having gotten a better work out. I know this bike is not cheap, but I like the way my mom put it to me:

Would you rather be out riding with your loved ones? This is a fantastic option for those who can't match the speed or stamina of the people they're riding with.
text_fidelity_b: sixthreezero Electric-Bicycles Around The Block Women's Ebike, 250/500 Watt Motor, 7-Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle with Rear Rack, 26" Wheels, Multiple Colors

Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway This is a great way to store 12 sets of polyhedral dice for D&D and similar games. I'm not sure if you strictly-speaking need waterproof storage for that, but while the O-ring may be overkill, the locking clasps and overall durability are a cut above what you usually find on parts organizers. This is never, ever going to come open unexpectedly and spill its precious contents all over the place!

With the dividers installed as shown in my photo, 8 areas hold a set of 7 polyhedral dice perfectly. Five of those will also hold a set of 12 six-sided dice. The four larger areas hold somewhat more; I have 10 d20's in one of them comfortably.

The downside of this approach is that you're certainly not going to sneak up on anyone while carrying one of these full of plastic/resin dice. And if you're into metal dice, or the sort of gemstone dice where each of them costs more than this whole container, then this probably isn't how you want to store them. (But you could probably pad them properly with a bit more work.)

Color of the O-ring seems to vary. I have two black and one blue, but the Plano part number stamped into it is the same for all three.

If you are the sort of person who needs to compactly and securely transport a lot of dice, this is the best way I've found to do it.
text_fidelity_b: Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway

text_fidelity_a:
J JACKCUBE DESIGN Skateboard Storage Holder - Skateboard Display Holder, Standing Storage, Skateboard Accessories for Portable Display or Skateboard Parking lot I am not a fan. The construction is simple, 6 total screws, 3 screws per leg. will take anyone, literally, a minute to assemble. Wood looks nice. Construction is sturdy and well made.

My problem:

It doesn't fit my skateboard. It seems to be the wheels. I have larger than I guess the average wheels. nothing ridiculous, a friend told me to get a bit larger diameter to assist in running over cracks/rocks and such while learning. so they have a larger diameter that what the most vanilla build would be. It created a tight fit. I had to really push into it a bit to get the skateboard on there. I could tell the larger size of wheels made the fit tighter. So that's a con, only works with specifically medium to small wheels. Or, perhaps trucks a bit longer. Either way, it requires a level of specificity I don't feel like looking in to.
Edit: Another reviewer mentioned low trucks. I suppose that could also be a cause. To reiterate, the trucks and wheels I am using are right off the shelf at a Zumiez. Standard, vanilla built skateboard, and this thing does not fit it.

I don't understand why the lean. In order to see the graphics of the skateboard, you have to face the stand backwards. So instead of looking at the solid wood design, you are looking at the legs and screws on the backside. Otherwise, you will be looking at the grip tape.

And the lean itself, while not extreme, why? There are less than 10 dollar plastic options that work well enough, and keep the board upright. So with the cheap plastic ones, not only is the board upright, it isn't reliant on trucks/wheel dimensions, and faces the graphics to be visible on display. For a product that is made of better material, I would have expected to be able to do that. The lean is just too awkward for my OCD.

I opted for the cheap 8 dollar plastic solution. Works well enough, board is upright, cool graphic showing, right in the corner of the room.
text_fidelity_b: J JACKCUBE DESIGN Skateboard Storage Holder - Skateboard Display Holder, Standing Storage, Skateboard Accessories for Portable Display or Skateboard Parking lot

text_fidelity_a:
Lifeline USA TNT Resistance Cable System I love this band workout system! Especially with the closed door attachment, this gives so much flexibility for a ton of different exercises. I'm able to work out all of my major muscle groups with this, and get a really full workout using this. I usually use only one or two bands, depending on the exercise, because the full 120 lbs of resistance with all 3 bands is usually too much for my workouts.

It's also light enough and compact enough that I can throw it in my suitcase when I travel. It's also way better than all the equipment in most hotel gyms. The bands are 5 feet long, and they stretch a lot, so even if you're really weak, then you can get a good workout with these, and not get frustrated.

At first, I was going to throw away the closed door attachment, and I'm super glad that I didn't. It's awesome! You put it on any door, and then it uses the strength of the frame and the hinges and the closed door for resistance. It's like you've attached the bands to a cement wall. It doesn't leave marks on the door, and works amazingly well.

The only bad thing is that it looks like it's out of stock, and may have been discontinued. You can still get the parts and piece this together, though.

Bodyguard Inverted Umbrella, Large Windproof Umbrellas for Rain & Sun, Compact Umbrella Reverse Umbrella with Reflective Stripe, Teflon Umbrella for Women Men, Travel Folding Umbrella with Cover Bag Every company seems to think that it can make the "next big thing" in umbrellas. It seems as though I've tried dozens of folding umbrellas that promise "this and that" but ultimately fail in one (or more) of the stated advantages. Most have some type of catastrophic failure after only a few uses, some so bad that they make the umbrella totally inoperable. So it was with some skepticism that I ordered this blue Bodyguard Travel Umbrella. It made a lot of promises on its product page -- but would it work as promised?

Finally I've found an umbrella that delivers on its promises. This Bodyguard Travel Umbrella sells for the impressive price of only $20.99, and puts a very useful collapsible umbrella in your hands. You can tell as soon as you pick it up that it is well-made and durable. It has some heft to it, snaps open with the push of a button, and collapses its canopy when you push the 'close' button. Then all you have to do is push the collapsed canopy down into the handle and your compact umbrella can be put into the supplied travel case.

The extra ribs give it additional strength when using it in the wind. It is probably more likely that it would be blown out of your hand than have the umbrella turn inside out on you. The handle is comfortable, fits my hand well, and has a wrist strap to keep it from the aforementioned potential flyaway. Yup, someone finally brought out a good one.
text_fidelity_b: Bodyguard Inverted Umbrella, Large Windproof Umbrellas for Rain & Sun, Compact Umbrella Reverse Umbrella with Reflective Stripe, Teflon Umbrella for Women Men, Travel Folding Umbrella with Cover Bag

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish I purchased this knife as a semi-impulse buy. I had been looking for a new edc for a couple months, however I was skeptic to stray away from my kershaw of 5 years.

After my initial purchase I read many mixed reviews, and after a month of carrying here are my thoughts.

PROS:
1) The low profile pocket clip doesn't scratch the crap out of my car paint as my kershaw did.
2) The metal is not as good as my kershaw, but it is VERY VERY close.
3) A ceramic hone works best after sharpening.
4) You can get this thing RAZOR sharp, but it dulls after a moderate amount of use.
5) It is SUPER light, and very fast.
6) Initially the opening mechanism is weird getting used to. However once you do, it is actually very easy to use.
7) The short blade does NOT impede its performance as I originally thought. You can think the belly of the knife for this, it adds a nice additional cutting surface.
8) The anodized aluminum is fairly slip resistant.
9) The thumb studs protrude enough for you to get a good open on it.
10) It is very sleek looking and the POP is an attention getter.
11) It is pretty ergonomic and it fits in the hand pretty well.

CONS:
1) It is difficult getting adjusted to the opening mechanism.
2) The "safety" makes me feel like this thing will jump open in my pocket if I don't have it turned on.... even though it probably wont.
3) I don't care for lock back knives as it impedes one handed use. I now can use it one handed though which took some practice.
4) The metal is odd, things you think would dull it won't.... but the things you don't think would will.. I.E. it cuts through weed eater string like a beast but a couple pieces of thin cardboard has this blade spent.
5) Tape and other adhesives stick to this blade BAD... My kershaw had a Teflon coating. Something I wished this one had.
6) the top of the pocket clip sticks up about 3/16 of an inch from the knife.... it is just odd to me. It doesn't really affect the functionality however.

Even though I questioned my purchase at first, I am very happy with my purchase. For this price you get a PERFECT edc knife. Just make sure that you have at least an 800-1200 grit diamond stone and a ceramic hone for quick sharpening.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish

With the semi-solid floor the boat is stable on the lakes; however, you cannot stand or dance as some reviewers claim. Solid floor allows it some degree of stability, but not enough to stand up or walk while being fully upright.

The hull materials and ores supplied are very good. Boat has a solid feel to it. When inflating it to the max, it become very firm- raft like.

For $220 this is an amazing deal. I would recommend this boat!

I had to try to canoe paddle the boat to shore and mend the plastic coupling with some duct tape! Upon returning home I checked the Intex's website for the replacement coupling; it is being sold for $4+ shipping. Can't blame the boat for the broken ore, plastic coupling is the cheapest part of this boat.

If you needed the manual it shows in detail. The scope takes (3) LR41w, AG3, CX41, or 392A. Any of these batteries will work. It has a windage adjustment but make sure to keep the screw loose while you make other adjustments first. If it’s tight then use the small Allen wrench to loosen. You have 4 different reticle patterns depending on your field of view.

Brightness is adjustable for both red and green reticles by pressing the button for brightness settings. The company listing says there are 5 brightness ettings. The included manual says nothing about any brightness settings. Here is what I experienced...Each time you turn the scope on to the color of choice, the default brightness starts at the lowest brightness and pressing up to 9 times then it goes back to default. Note: after turning off, it does not remember your last brightness setting, but hey… this is still a nice feature!

After you’re done using the scope you have to press both the red and green buttons to turn off. You can see in the company’s listed picture how it shows the off button with arrows pointing downward on both red/green buttons.

My final thoughts are this scope is of good value. It is also waterproof and shockproof according to the manual.

Serengeti Erice 8504 Having gotten several years excellent use from glass-lensed Serengeti drivers and 555nm polarized sunglasses, when the frames on those finally broke it was time for replacements. I decided on the plastic lensed, more wrap around styles. First, I got the Maestrale in Drivers Polarized. Really love that one! I wanted something neutral for bright, clear days, and also when doing photography, so thought I'd try the newer Erice in the CPG lens. I will compare the two...

The main attraction is that the Erice is more open on top, so ought to ventilate and not fog up as much as the Maestrale. Surprisingly, it is not any better in practical use! Still fogs up easily in certain situations. Also, my eyebrows generate a lot of oil, and I have to clean the Erice as much or more than the Maestrale. The eye-side of the lens on the Erice is coated to reduce reflection, but this also makes it more "sticky" to clean.

On the other hand, the Maestrale, with it's closed bar across the top, really hugs the eyebrows and keeps the sun from peeking of the top.

The frame is thicker and rounds outward a bit more than the Maestrale. Sometimes this interferes with winter hats, etc. Also, it weighs a bit more, so won't stay on top of my head as well as the Maestrale.

Ultimately, I like the Maestrale better and hope they keep it in the line for many years to come.

By the way, both units come with the same semi-hard case and cleaning cloth, and both are made in Japan. They cost me about the same, too.
text_fidelity_b: Serengeti Erice 8504

text_fidelity_a:
REDESS 11 Pack Exercise Resistance Bands with Handles Exercise Stretch Fitness Home Set Include 5 Stackable Exercise Bands with Carry Bag, Handles, Legs Ankle Straps & Door Anchor FINAL UPDATE - I ordered a Fitfort set, which has the same function as this package but doesn't seem destined to fail. I donated this set to Salvation Army the day Fitfort arrived. End of story.

UPDATE - After 4 months, the nylon bands on one handle failed. I'm improvising with rope earlier, the attachment to one band had to be fixed, and the black band has now torn. Was this worth four months' gym membership?

After one use, I find this adequate. I find good all-around routines, inlcuding one for straps, on darebee.

This kit provides a lot more resistance than the latex straps I'd been using. And the concept of being able to adjust your resistance by combining the five bands is good in principle. It's clear this will work better if you have good technique—slow, smooth movements, not jerky Yanks. But the small problems add up:

The concept is cool, but not unique. Post-COVID, there are a lot of these packs available, many for $10-15 less. Consider them!

Many reviews cite the handles as a weak point, and it's clear they will fail in time. They lasted fine through the first workout. (See below.)

These bands give different levels of resistance, but I'm not sure how much. There are 2 contradictory weight schemes in the Amazon posting (diff weights, diff color). Hint: blue is stronger than green. Also, I have no confidence that the numerical values are right. Is black really 40/50 pounds? Either I'm really strong...

Reviewers also reported snapped bands, and maybe it might be good to warm them up with a stretch before your workout. I believe the black and blue will snap if I stretch from from the floor to overhead, no I will have to kneel for military presses. And move smoothly thru your exercises, don't jerk or yank. It's better form, and will avoid snapping.

The Velcro ankle straps? Ha! Loop them through and they are secure!

UPDATE after 3 months: this set works, but it's not durable. One of the handles will tear, and then I'll have to re-sew it. The black band came loose from one of its hooks, and I re-fit it. The convenient carrying sack is fraying, like the ankle bands. This has been a lifeline during the lockdown that made my gym unsafe, but this is not a long-term fitness tool. It just won't last.

(CAUTION - the high rating for this set is because the reviews are mixed with what must be a very good beanie. Users of this set average 1-2 stars.)
text_fidelity_b: REDESS 11 Pack Exercise Resistance Bands with Handles Exercise Stretch Fitness Home Set Include 5 Stackable Exercise Bands with Carry Bag, Handles, Legs Ankle Straps & Door Anchor

text_fidelity_a:
LifeStraw Flex Advanced Water Filter with Gravity Bag - Removes Lead, Bacteria, Parasites and Chemicals Blue, 1 gal This kit comes with a LifeStraw, a backwashing syringe, and a soft-touch bottle. They recommend using the syringe to backwash the LifeStraw once before using and a minimum of twice a day during use to prevent the filter from getting clogged and to help remove any trapped particles. The LifeStraw is 6.5" long, 1.5" across, and has a two stage water filter. The first stage is a hollow fiber membrane filter that removes 99.999999% of bacteria and 99.999% of protozoa. It is good for 2,000 liters (500 gallons). The stage one filter will no longer filter water when the product has reached the end of its working life. The second stage is a replaceable active carbon fiber capsule that reduces lead and chlorine, improves taste, reduces bad odor and organic chemical matter. It lasts 100 liters (25 gallons). Both ends of the LifeStraw unscrew for easy access to the filters or to allow it to dry out when not in use.

You start by backwashing the LifeStraw, which is fairly simple to do and does not require clean water. I then filled the soft-touch bottle with water and screwed the LifeStraw in place. The first 5 to 10 sips through the LifeStraw tasted very nasty and I spit it out. Then the water started tasting clean. It was not difficult to suck the water through the straw when the filters are new. Evidently, it gets harder as the filter life gets near its end, so you might not get a full 500 gallons use in real life. Also, you can squeeze the soft-touch bottle to force water through the LifeStraw, which I was able to do.

I set the soft-touch bottle down on its side as there is no way to set it (or hang it) upright. I came back 10 minutes later to find a puddle of water under the joint where the soft body joins with the harder material of the neck of the bottle. The leak was not where the LifeStraw screwed into the bottle but was a flaw in the bottle. You can also simply place the end of the LifeStraw in a cup of water and suck in the water, which I have been doing since this incident. It can also be used with a gravity filter, a hydration bladder, or screwed into the top of any standard plastic bottle.

I was disappointed that the soft-touch bottle leaked and that there was no way to secure it upright when filled with water. The LifeStraw seems to work fine, and I've been wanting to try one for it years. The LifeStraw is a small enough size to be easily portable for use when hiking, but the syringe is nearly as big as the LifeStraw and so doubles the amount of room needed to pack both.
text_fidelity_b: LifeStraw Flex Advanced Water Filter with Gravity Bag - Removes Lead, Bacteria, Parasites and Chemicals Blue, 1 gal

text_fidelity_a:
UVPaqlite Tooblite I recently bought several UVPaqlite items, and have had some time to test them out. Out of the 4 items I purchased, this was reasonably impressive. With fair exposure to light, it will glow strong for 10 minutes. Around the 15 minute mark, it has faded a bit, but is still bright enough that you can still read with it in total darkness, with adjusted eyes. By 60 minutes, it's faintly visible in a dark room, with your eyes adjusted. Even by 90 minutes, it's still faintly visible, but only just barely.

Out of the 4 UVPaqlite items I purchased, this didn't glow as strong or last as long as the UVPaqlite packets - however, that seemed natural, given its tubular design (less surface area exposed to the viewer). The clear resin had a lot of bubbles, which seemed to diffuse the glow a bit - making for a more even light, but also limiting its range. However, the tubular design is also its biggest strength. Compared to the UVPaqlite packets - which are fairly rugged in their own right - this seems much more durable, as well as convenient to carry or mount. As such, I mounted this next to my quick-release home shotgun mount. In the event the lights immediately go out, I can quickly - even before my eyes have adjusted - find my flashlight and unlock the shotgun, should I need it.

If you need stronger and longer lasting light, I recommend the UVPaqlite vacuum-sealed packets. Both the [[ASIN:B00698NBYE UVPaqlite Medium]] and [[ASIN:B00698HB1I UVPaqlite Mini]] out-performed the Tooblites I bought, as far as effective brightness. However, consider that the Tooblite shape is more convenient for certain tasks. As well, while these "charge and glow" phosphorescent products have their purposes, they can't replace a flashlight or chemiluminescence glow stick when you need on-demand light. So, consider what you might use them for, before purchasing.
text_fidelity_b: UVPaqlite Tooblite

It starts to, the device recognizes and displays the check mark, the app goes to finish it, gets to around 60%, hangs, dies, start over.  Repeat, repeat, repeat.  Support was clueless.  I have decided to return it.  This is the third FitBit I’ve owned, the second to have issue while newer.  I suspect I will move on to another brand.  Great when they work, but they seem to release before the devices are ready and I am tired of paying  to be a beta tester.

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick I've previously owned a Klymit V without the "Luxe," but a piece of the one valve it had broke off in short order. This Klymit V Luxe has valves which *appear* to me to have fewer fiddly parts, and there are two of them--more on why that's good in a moment!

First off, these pads have a smart design. Although there is no railing per say, the Vs help to keep you on them which is good news if you do not stay in one place on a bed. The material keeps the air inside from feeling cold (and presumably from drinking in too much of the earth's cold).

The primary use I gave my original V was as a buffer between me and an extremely ill-suited new mattress while I desperately shopped for solutions. And although I've been a backpacker in the past, sadly, my primary intended use for the Static V Luxe is to act as a buffering layer when I need to sleep on other people's mattresses. I have considerable back health issues, and this padding is incredibly helpful for when I cannot be on my own mattress. I purchased this size this time because the original V is so much smaller than a twin bed that it was downright silly trying to use it for my purpose. Also I use a body pillow and change positions a lot. This will clearly be nicer for managing nights out of my own bed.

Now I saw someone complaining about the two valves because they are confusing. This person has probably never experienced the downsides of only having one valve for letting air out of a mattress. Sure, you need to be certain that the valve you are not blowing into is closed so that the mattress can properly inflate, but oh, my word, it is soooooo much easier to get the air out of this mattress pad! I could almost never get my original V small enough to properly stick into its dry sack. But this larger V luxe easily packs up smaller than I could get the original V to go. Ok, so maybe "easy" is relative. You do need to open both valves, roll it down from bottom to top, open it up again, fold a few times, and roll once more to get it maximally small. But it actually works and stuffs in the drysack.

I hope if you're reading this that you have more adventurous uses afoot, but I do recommend this Static V Luxe and wish I'd had one back when I was a backpacker!
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick
